interpretations: For each gender represented among customers with an invoice, treating SQL NULL as its own group, count distinct invoiced orders. Return the average count and average excess above the overall unweighted group average for groups strictly above that average.

For each gender present in Customers, treating SQL NULL as its own group and assigning zero to groups with no invoiced orders, return those same two averages for groups strictly above the overall unweighted group average.

For each gender represented among customers with an invoice, combine NULL and blank gender values into one missing-gender group, then return those same two averages for groups strictly above the overall unweighted group average.

For each gender present in Customers, combine NULL and blank gender values into one missing-gender group and assign zero to groups with no invoiced orders, then return those same two averages for groups strictly above the overall unweighted group average.
queries:
WITH gender_counts AS (
  SELECT c.gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count
  FROM Customers AS c
  JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY c.gender
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_count) AS average_count
  FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT
  AVG(gc.order_count) AS average_count,
  AVG(gc.order_count - ov.average_count) AS average_excess
FROM gender_counts AS gc
CROSS JOIN overall AS ov
WHERE gc.order_count > ov.average_count

WITH customer_counts AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        NULLIF(TRIM(c.gender), '') AS gender,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN i.invoice_number IS NOT NULL THEN o.order_id END) AS invoiced_orders
    FROM Customers AS c
    LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
),
gender_averages AS (
    SELECT gender, AVG(invoiced_orders) AS average_invoiced_orders
    FROM customer_counts
    GROUP BY gender
),
overall_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(average_invoiced_orders) AS overall_group_average
    FROM gender_averages
)
SELECT
    g.gender,
    g.average_invoiced_orders,
    a.overall_group_average
FROM gender_averages AS g
CROSS JOIN overall_average AS a
WHERE g.average_invoiced_orders > a.overall_group_average
